title: Softmax Jacobian
prompt: The softmax Jacobian is J(i,j) = s_i*(δ(i,j) − s_j). At logits z = [0, 0] (so s = [1/2, 1/2]), compute J.
recap:
For softmax s = softmax(z), the Jacobian is J(i, j) = sᵢ(δᵢⱼ − sⱼ): diagonal sᵢ(1 − sᵢ), off-diagonal −sᵢsⱼ. It is symmetric and each row sums to 0 (softmax outputs sum to 1).

Example — z = [0, 0] → s = [1/2, 1/2], so J = [[1/4, −1/4], [−1/4, 1/4]].

With cross-entropy it collapses to the p − y gradient. Reference: Bishop, Pattern Recognition and ML, §4.3.4.
